analysis.lean: No real edge on the side or total; the market is close to fair, so this is a pass or a very small lean to Atlanta at home.
why: Our ratings project ATL by +3.7 and the market has ATL -1.0. Blended at 0.20 weight that is +1.5, a small gap, and the sample is only 4-5 games per team.
Adjusted net rating: ATL +3.1 vs CLE +1.4, a modest edge to the home side. ATL's raw 120.2 scored / 115.2 allowed is skewed by the 128-81 win at CHA.
The projected total of 237.2 is just under the posted 238.0 (blend 237.8), so there is no total edge. Pace is 104.6 and 105.6, with a projection of 106.4.
Both teams are on the second night of a back-to-back, so rest is even and gives no adjustment. The schedule spot is already handled by the projection where applicable.

ATL's defense gives up a 0.310 ORB% and 0.178 TOV% forced by CLE... correction: ATL's defense allows a 0.31 ORB% (weak on the glass), while CLE's offense grabs 0.275. That helps CLE's second chances, but it is early-season noise.
risks: Samples of 4 and 5 games make every rating tentative.
Back-to-back for both teams could mean minutes management or fatigue; CLE starters average 33.0 min, which is a heavy load on the second night.
Officials are not posted, so there is no crew read on totals or free throws.
matchups: CLE shoots 42% of its shots from three and ATL allows 42% (league average), so there is no clear three-point edge for either side.
ATL allows centers +8% assists per minute, which is a small positive for Jarrett Allen or Mobley as a playmaker, but small sample.
verify: Check the final injury report for both teams near tip, especially for CLE, which lists no injuries.
Confirm that no rest or minutes limits were announced for the CLE starters on the back-to-back.
Check whether the officials get posted and whether the spread moves off -1.0.

judgment.why: Both teams are on the second night of a back-to-back, the market is a near pick'em (ATL -1.0, fair home cover 0.50), and the 4-5 game samples are too small to justify moving off the market price.

analysis.lean: No strong lean: the market is efficient here, and if forced, NOP -6.0 is a coin flip with a small tilt to SAC +6.
why: Our blended margin is NOP +5.7 against a -6.0 line, so the spread gap is about 0.3 points.
Blended total is 236.1 against 236.5, which is no edge on the total.
SAC's defense is poor: 125.5 allowed per game raw, 115.1 adjusted, and opponents shoot 0.579 eFG against it. That supports NOP scoring.
NOP is on a back-to-back and without Yves Missi (1.5 points of value, already in the projection). Both teams are 0-4, so the ratings are heavily shrunk and the samples are small.

NOP's offense takes 42% of its shots at the rim, and SAC allows 32% of opponent shots at the rim. SAC's shot-quality allowed is 1.14 actual points per shot against 1.083 expected, so it is leaking beyond its shot mix.
risks: NOP is on the second night of a back-to-back, with Poole day-to-day (ankle) and Missi out.
Four-game samples mean the ratings and tendencies can swing a lot.
NOP has lost close games (119-120, 120-123), so it may be better than its 0-4 record, but that is not enough to move a number.
matchups: SAC's Sabonis (16.5 reb per game) against a NOP frontcourt missing Missi: NOP allows centers +8% rebounds and +10% points per minute, which helps Sabonis.
NOP guards (Murray, Fears) against SAC's defense, which allows guards +7% threes and +6% assists.
verify: The packet's projection credits SAC with Keegan Murray 'back' (+0.6 points), but the injury report lists him Out for 10-14 days. The projection may be about 0.6 points too kind to SAC, so confirm his status.
Check Jordan Poole's status (day-to-day, ankle) and any late NOP scratches.
Check the final line and total before betting, and for officials once they are posted.

judgment.why: The blended projection (NOP +5.7, total 236.1) is almost the same as the market (-6.0, 236.5), both teams are 0-4 on tiny samples, and I see no edge beyond the market's fair price.

analysis.lean: No strong lean: the market is efficient here, and the Portland -7.5 and total 232.5 are both close to fair.
why: Our projection is POR +7.0 and the blend is +7.4, versus a market spread of -7.5, so there is no meaningful gap on the side.
The projected total is 230.1 (blend 232.1) against the market 232.5, a slight lean under at most, which is not enough to act on.
POR's adjusted net is +4.0 against MEM's -0.8, but MEM's raw 116.8/107.0 and POR's raw 129.3/110.7 come from 4 and 3 games, so the adjusted ratings are heavily shrunk.

POR's shot profile is strong (35% rim, 49% of shots from three, expected 1.109 points per shot), but its actual 1.076 is below that, and MEM's defense allows slightly more than expected (1.107 vs 1.089).
Absences and schedule are already in the projection (net -0.3 margin, +0.1 total), so I made no further adjustment.
risks: The samples are tiny (POR 3 games, MEM 4), and POR's 124-83 win over PHX inflates its raw numbers.
The two teams' rest differs (MEM 2 days, POR 1 day), but that is already counted in the projection.
matchups: POR allows centers +9% points and +20% threes per minute, which could help MEM's bigs; Edey is back at 21.3 min but averages only 6.0 pts.
MEM allows guards +8% threes per minute, a good spot for Lillard (4.0 threes per game).
verify: Confirm the final injury report for both teams near tip; MEM lists no injuries.
The Youngblood note refers to a Lakers game, so it may be stale; Sharpe is out long term.
Check that the -7.5 spread and 232.5 total have not moved before betting.

judgment.why: Our blended margin (+7.4) and total (232.1) sit almost on the market's -7.5 and 232.5, and the samples are only 3-4 games, so I have no edge beyond the fair price.

lessons: Early sample (49 graded picks). Treat every rating as tentative.
Points props are 10-3 with cushion and role signals, but 13 picks is too few to trust. Keep them as normal plays and don't scale them up yet.
Assists, rebounds and threes are 2-10 combined, and rebounds and threes are 0-3 each. Too small to be a rule; lean skip on thin-signal ones.
Picks with no signal are 1-6 and beat the close by -1.6%. Lean skip when no cushion, role, matchup or pace signal backs the pick.
The model said 57.2% overall and 63.5% on 8-12% edges, which went 2-6. Be wary of large edges; don't scale up on size alone.
